chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from his brother Al Hassan, from Zur’at, from Abu Baseer who said,

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'We are narrating about the souls of the Believer that they are in the craws of green birds grazing in the Paradise, and sheltering to the lamps beneath the Throne'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No. Then, what is in the craws of birds?' I said, 'So where are they?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'In a Garden like in the (shape of) bodies in the Paradise'.
ai.seo_question: Where are the souls of believers located after death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) corrects the popular folk belief that souls reside in the craws of green birds, affirming instead that they inhabit a garden in the Barzakh that mirrors the form of their physical bodies. This clarification highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of bodily identity in the intermediate realm, distinguishing between metaphorical descriptions and the actual ontological state of the soul before resurrection.
